MagicBlock Blitz · Solana

Two traders. Two tokens.
Neither can see the other's book.

A five-minute duel. Each player picks any pump.fun or Jupiter market and goes long or short on it. Both positions live on a MagicBlock Ephemeral Rollup behind an on-chain access-control list, so the fills are sealed while they can still be traded against, and public the moment they cannot. At the buzzer both tapes are written to Solana and the pot pays out.

What the rollup is actually doing

A fill on a rollup and a fill on a validator look identical from outside, so the project ships a check that asks both clusters where a real fill went. These are its four assertions, and the speeds the page measures live.

npm run check:er — and /proof, measured on this machine
ClaimResult
Position owner while the round runsthe delegation program — the base layer has given custody away
Fill signature in the rollup ledgerfound, at a real slot
Same signature on the base layerabsent — it never happened there
Rollup block rate80.8 slots/s against the base layer's 2.1 — a 9.5× speedup
Sealed position, read anonymouslyREFUSED
Same account shape, no permissionSERVED — the control row, because a door shut for everybody is not access control
Owner, with a signed tokentheir own position, and not their opponent's
Network fees for one whole duel0.000530 SOL — 0.265% of a 0.20◎ pot

The life of one duel

Every base-layer transaction touching either position, oldest first. This is a real sequence read back from the chain, which is why it is numbered — the order is the delegation story.

  1. Join matchescrowed on Solana
  2. Create position permissionan ACL account per position
  3. Create position permissionone for each player
  4. Delegate position permissionso the rollup can read the ACL
  5. Delegate position permissionboth sides
  6. Delegate position to ERSolana hands custody to the delegation program
  7. Delegate position to ERboth sides
  8. Process undelegationthe buzzer: ownership comes home
  9. Process undelegationboth sides
  10. Settle matchPnL compared, pot paid, public tape written

Check it without a wallet

Every claim above reproduces from a clean checkout against the local stack. No wallet, no account, no faucet.

npm run check:erWhere the trade executed: delegated custody, the signature in the rollup's ledger, and its absence from the base layer's.
npm run check:gateThe privacy proof — a sealed position refused, the same account shape without a permission served as the control.
npm run check:shortA real negative position, the margin cap, and a liquidation announced without leaking what was behind it.
npm run check:tapeEvery settled tape on the cluster replayed onto the chain's own PnL, and the impact previewer against every recorded execution price.
npm run checkAll seventeen suites.
cd chain && anchor test --skip-local-validator27 on-chain tests, 2 pending. Includes the negative case: a fill that succeeds on the rollup is rejected on L1 while the account is delegated.

What this does not prove

  • Enforcement is proved; attestation is not. The rollup sits behind a query-filtering service that reads the permission program and really refuses — the control row above is how you can tell it is checking the ACL rather than being shut. What is missing is a TEE to attest that the gate is the process we say it is, so /proof carries two rows, and only the second says NO.
  • Local cluster, not devnet. The program is 798,056 bytes; deploying it needs roughly 6–10 devnet SOL and every faucet path refused. The program ID in the repo is stated as local rather than dressed up as a deployment.
  • VRF is requested, never fulfilled. The request lands and the VRF program accepts it, but the queues this validator preloads name devnet oracle identities we do not hold keys for. Nothing simulates a draw, and no UI is built on one that cannot resolve.
  • Positions are virtual inventory. No SPL moves during a round and no fill is routed to pump.fun or a Jupiter swap — a public swap print would hand the opponent the wallet, the mint and the size the fog exists to hide. Those feeds price the round; each player's own constant-product book fills it.
Recorded against the local five-layer stack — base layer, ephemeral rollup, read gate, market proxy, and the production web export.
